text: Refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of your code without changing what it does. Think of it like reorganizing a messy closet: you rearrange your clothes and shoes, but you still wear the same items. The main goal is to make the code easier to read and understand. This involves renaming confusing variables, breaking large functions into smaller ones, and removing duplicated logic. By doing this regularly, you reduce "technical debt"—the hidden cost of taking shortcuts that make future changes harder. Cleaner code means fewer bugs and faster development, so refactoring is a smart habit, not just extra work.
